title: Rivet: intellect + will; justifying faith an aggregated habit
source_text: XVI. Rivetus similiter proprium & speciale fidei justificantis subjectum in homine, est non solum intellectus, sed etiam voluntas. Notitia enim, inquit, & assensus ad intellectum pertinent, fiducia autem ad voluntatem. Nec ad justificationem sufficit, ut intellectus comprehendat quae Dei sunt, nisi voluntas eadem apprehendat & amplectatur, non solum in thesi, sed etiam in hypothesi. Et postea monet fidem, quatenus est justificans, Non esse habitum unum numero simplicem absolute, sed esse unum habitum aggregatione, & quodammodo compositum ex duobus, qui coordinatione tantum unum sunt, nempe quatenus fides simul involvit habitum existentem in voluntate, quo voluntas prompta sit ad credendum & confidendum Deo, quomodo duo habitus possunt esse una virtus, & duae res unus actus, & multae scientiae dicuntur habitus, tantum coordinatione unum, &c. In Synopsi purioris Theologiae, Disput. 31. Thes. 14. & 16.
pass_a_gloss: Rivet likewise: the proper and special subject of justifying faith in man is not only intellect but also will. For knowledge and assent, he says, belong to intellect, but trust to the will. Nor does it suffice for justification that the intellect comprehend the things of God unless the will also apprehends and embraces them, not only in thesis but also in hypothesis. And afterward he notes that faith, insofar as justifying, is not one numerically simple habit absolutely, but one habit by aggregation, somehow composed of two that are one only by coordination — namely insofar as faith simultaneously involves a habit existing in the will by which the will is ready to believe and trust God — just as two habits can be one virtue, and two things one act, and many sciences are called a habit as one only by coordination, etc. (Synopsis purioris Theologiae, Disp. 31 theses 14 and 16).
pass_b_english: Rivet: justifying faith's subject is intellect and will (knowledge/assent vs trust).
Justifying faith is one habit by aggregation/coordination, not one simple numerical habit.

choices.why: Will-side of justifying faith for Rivet.
